html:
The Tequesta were an Indigenous people of the southeast Atlantic coast of Florida, centred on the mouth of the Miami River. They lived by fishing, catching turtles and manatees, and gathering roots, palm berries and shellfish; they did not farm.

Their towns were tied to, and sometimes under, the powerful Calusa of the southwest coast. In 1567 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés set up a Jesuit mission and a small fort among them, but it did not last. The Miami Circle, a ring of holes cut in the rock at the river mouth and found in 1998, is linked to them. Disease and slave raids from the north wore them down, and by the mid-1700s the last groups had left, some for Cuba. Their neighbours included the Ais and the Mayaimi.
